statement: The x01 neutral-rename workpack's owns: line ('Cargo.toml [workspace.package] + crates/*/Cargo.toml [package] name fields + the two name.rs consts ONLY') was ALREADY 90% satisfied before this lane ran: every crate [package] name and enforcer-cli's [[bin]] name were already the neutral enforcer-* form (a3e660c's arc-22 skeleton pass had landed them), and BINARY_NAME was already "enforcer". The only real deltas were: root Cargo.toml's repository URL (github.com/ocentra/ocentra-enforcer.git -> .../enforcer.git) and enforcer-mcp's SERVER_NAME const ("ocentra-enforcer" -> "enforcer"). The CANONICAL_TOOL_PREFIX/LEGACY_ALIAS_PREFIX consts, which the skeleton had co-located in name.rs, had to be RELOCATED (not deleted) into crate::aliases because they are 1:1 keyed to crate::registry::CANONICAL_TOOLS' still-ocentra_enforcer_*-named literal table, which x01 does not own or rewrite -- leaving them in name.rs would have made x01's own owned-surface grep gate fail against its own file.
why: A future rename-adjacent pack (x03 rename-migration, or whoever eventually flips crate::registry::CANONICAL_TOOLS to a neutral prefix) needs to know that crate::aliases::CANONICAL_TOOL_PREFIX/LEGACY_ALIAS_PREFIX are the mechanism-owned copies (not name.rs's identity const) -- if someone 'cleans up' by re-merging them into name.rs without also renaming the registry's tool-literal family in the same pass, they will silently reintroduce a rust_rules/ocentra_enforcer literal into x01's owned grep-gate surface and break neutral-rename-grep-clean.
howToApply: When x03 (or any pack) renames crate::registry::CANONICAL_TOOLS off the ocentra_enforcer_* family, move crate::aliases::CANONICAL_TOOL_PREFIX's value in that same commit, and only then consider re-deriving it from enforcer_mcp::name::SERVER_NAME if the two are meant to be identical again. Do not add the tool-family prefix back into name.rs as a literal without doing the registry rename in the same change.

evidence.ref: crates/enforcer-mcp/src/name.rs (SERVER_NAME only, post x01); crates/enforcer-mcp/src/aliases.rs (CANONICAL_TOOL_PREFIX="ocentra_enforcer", LEGACY_ALIAS_PREFIX="rust_rules", both pub(crate)); crates/enforcer-mcp/src/registry.rs CANONICAL_TOOLS (unchanged, out of x01 owns:)

statement: x01's grep-gate proof (neutral-rename-grep-clean) is scoped field-by-field, not whole-file, for crates/*/Cargo.toml: only the [package] name / [[bin]] name lines are scanned there (a stray token in a sibling-owned field like enforcer-mcp/Cargo.toml's `description`, which still says 'ocentra_enforcer_*/rust_rules_*', is out of scope per the workpack's explicit 'Coordinate only the name field' note and a01's ownership of manifest structure). Root Cargo.toml and the two name.rs files ARE scanned whole-file, matching the workpack's broader 'workspace-level name/description/repository product strings' checklist line for the root manifest.
why: Without this field-scoping distinction, the grep-gate test (crates/enforcer-mcp/tests/neutral_rename.rs) would false-fail forever on enforcer-mcp's own Cargo.toml description field, which is legitimately owned by a sibling concern (crate manifest content) and references the STILL-CURRENT internal tool-name family (crate::registry::CANONICAL_TOOLS), not a residual product-identity bug.
howToApply: If a future pack widens the grep gate to whole-file scanning of crates/*/Cargo.toml, it must first land the registry.rs tool-name-family rename (x03's job), or the gate will immediately regress on enforcer-mcp/Cargo.toml's description string.

evidence.ref: cargo test -p enforcer-mcp --test neutral_rename -- neutral_rename_grep_clean passed; manual grep -inE against crates/*/Cargo.toml showed enforcer-mcp/Cargo.toml:7 description field as the only whole-file residual, explicitly excluded by field-scoped scan
